    Ordinary traces of E_7 and E_8 in characteristic two (Appendix B) #

    characteristic-two-mesh-calculations.tex: "Apply Lemma A.6(1) in characteristic two. For a = yx³ and b = yx⁴, its block relations and 3[ab] = 0 give [a²W] = 0 (W ≠ 1), [abW] = [baW] (W ≠ 1), [ab] = 0, [b^q] = 0 (q ≥ 2). Words with two a's and at least three blocks vanish by bringing the a's together. With exactly one a, only ab² can remain: abʳ has word degree greater than fourteen for r ≥ 3. For the one-y words, the identities 3[yx²] = 0 and 5[yx⁴] = 0 still hold, whereas no vanishing follows from 2[yx] = 2[yx³] = 0. Thus the ordinary positive trace is spanned by yx, yx³, (yx³)², (yx³)(yx⁴)² in word degrees 2, 4, 8, 14."

    We run the induction of Lemma A.6 on the number of y's in a fixed word degree n, with values in a subgroup A of the target containing the candidate class of degree n (all_mem).

    Prop

    The hypotheses in characteristic two.

    • x5 : x ^ 5 = 0
    • y3 : y ^ 3 = 0
    • d1 : y * y + y * x + x * y + x * x = 0
    • two : 2 = 0
    • rot (p q : S) : tr (p * q) = tr (q * p)
    • xp (q : ℕ) : 1 ≤ q → tr (x ^ q) = 0
    • ty : tr y = 0
    • ty2 : tr (y * y) = 0
